title: Proximal ureter blood supply: branches of the renal artery
vignette: A 55-year-old man with a history of end-stage renal disease due to polycystic kidney disease is scheduled to undergo living-donor kidney transplantation. To harvest the donor kidney, a laparoscopic left nephrectomy is performed on the living donor. During the procedure, the left kidney and proximal ureter are visualized, and a short segment of proximal ureter is harvested with its surrounding periureteric tissue preserved to maintain blood supply after transplantation. Which of the following arteries normally supplies blood to this portion of the ureter?

clues.text: short segment of proximal ureter is harvested
clues.note: The PROXIMAL (upper) ureter receives its blood supply from branches of the RENAL artery; only a short, well-vascularized segment is taken to avoid distal ischemia.

whatMatters: The PROXIMAL ureter is supplied by branches of the RENAL ARTERY. (The middle/distal ureter has a variable, anastomotic supply from the gonadal, common/internal iliac, and superior vesical arteries.) In transplant, a short proximal segment is used because it is best vascularized. Answer E.
strategy: Map ureteral blood supply by level: PROXIMAL = renal artery; middle = variable (gonadal, common/internal iliac, aortic); distal = internal iliac branches, especially superior vesical artery. The stem specifies the PROXIMAL ureter -> renal artery. Reject the common iliac, internal iliac, and superior vesical (supply more DISTAL segments), lumbar arteries (supply the posterior body wall), and phrenic artery (supplies the diaphragm/adrenal).

eliminations.label: Common iliac artery - more distal segment
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a branch contributing to the MIDDLE ureter's variable supply. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it supplies a more distal segment, not the proximal ureter harvested here. ✅ Correct if: mid-ureteral blood supply.

eliminations.label: Internal iliac artery - distal ureter
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: source (with the superior vesical) of the DISTAL ureteral supply. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it supplies the pelvic (distal) ureter, not the proximal segment near the kidney. ✅ Correct if: distal ureteral supply.

eliminations.label: Lumbar arteries - body wall, not ureter
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: paired aortic branches to the lumbar vertebrae and posterior body wall. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: they supply the body wall, not the ureter. ✅ Correct if: posterior abdominal wall/vertebral supply.

eliminations.label: Phrenic artery - diaphragm/adrenal
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the inferior phrenic artery (from the aorta) supplying the diaphragm and superior adrenal. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it supplies the diaphragm/adrenal gland, not the ureter. ✅ Correct if: diaphragmatic/adrenal blood supply.

eliminations.label: Superior vesical artery - distal ureter/bladder
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an internal iliac branch supplying the DISTAL ureter and bladder. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it supplies the distal ureter, not the proximal segment. ✅ Correct if: distal ureteral/bladder supply.

reasoning: The proximal ureter lies near the kidney and renal hilum
Its blood supply comes from branches of the renal artery
Only a short, well-vascularized proximal segment is harvested to avoid distal ischemia
mechanism: The URETER receives a SEGMENTAL, level-dependent blood supply. The PROXIMAL (abdominal/upper) ureter is supplied by branches of the RENAL ARTERY. The MIDDLE ureter has a variable, ANASTOMOTIC supply from the gonadal (testicular/ovarian) artery, the abdominal aorta, and the common/internal iliac arteries. The DISTAL (pelvic) ureter is supplied by branches of the INTERNAL ILIAC system, especially the SUPERIOR VESICAL artery. Importantly, the proximal/abdominal ureter receives its arterial branches MEDIALLY, whereas the pelvic ureter receives them LATERALLY (a surgical principle to preserve blood supply during dissection). In kidney transplantation, only a SHORT segment of donor ureter is preserved (kept with its periureteric tissue) because the DISTAL ureter is prone to ISCHEMIA once separated from its native pelvic collateral supply - distal ureteral ischemia/necrosis can cause urine leak in the early post-transplant period. The distractors (common/internal iliac, superior vesical) supply more distal segments, and the lumbar and phrenic arteries supply the body wall and diaphragm/adrenal, respectively.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid/anatomy > ureteral blood supply: proximal = renal artery; middle = variable (gonadal, aortic, common/internal iliac); distal = internal iliac/superior vesical; proximal branches enter medially, distal laterally; transplant distal ureteral ischemia risk.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Proximal ureter = renal artery; distal = internal iliac/superior vesical.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on proximal vs distal ureter, renal artery branches, internal iliac/superior vesical, or gonadal artery? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Common/internal iliac and superior vesical supply the distal ureter; lumbar = body wall; phrenic = diaphragm/adrenal.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: ureter blood supply - proximal (renal artery), middle (gonadal/iliac/aortic), distal (internal iliac/superior vesical).

keywords.back: Internal iliac branches (esp. superior vesical artery)
Abdominal ureter medially; pelvic ureter laterally
Crosses anterior to the ureter ('water under the bridge' concept for uterine/ductus)

firstAid.detail: Anatomy > distal = internal iliac/superior vesical; middle = variable.
Uro > preserve short proximal segment; distal ischemia risk.

memoryHook: Top of the ureter drinks from the kidney's own artery (renal); the bottom sips from the pelvic (internal iliac) vessels - so a proximal segment lives on the renal artery.
